walls.source: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Aalst' (https://id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140017)
walls.note: Aalst: wall of c. 1200 on both banks of the Dender, given bastions in the late 16th and 17th c.; still standing in 1650 and razed after Turenne took the town in 1667. Traced from the tree-lined rampart line (Wallenring) on the Ferraris map (1777). Gate names not verified.

landmarks.y1650: Aldermen's house of c. 1225, oldest in the Low Countries, with its belfry tower of 1460; on the UNESCO list of belfries.
landmarks.src: nl.wikipedia 'Schepenhuis (Aalst)'; UNESCO 'Belfries of Belgium and France'

landmarks.n: Landhuis van het Land van Aalst
landmarks.y1650: Seat of the States of the Land van Aalst on the Grote Markt (present front partly later).
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Aalst' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140017)

landmarks.y1650: Collegiate church begun c. 1480 to a vast plan and never finished: no nave or tower beyond the transept (Rubens's altarpiece of St Roch hangs here from 1623-26).

landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Aalst' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140017)

landmarks.y1650: Printer Dirk Martens (d. 1534) printed the first book in the Low Countries here in 1473; a statue is 19th c.
